column1: Figure 15-2 graphs the relationship between inflation pt and output Yt described by this equation. We call this upward-sloping curve the dynamic aggregate supply curve, or DAS. The dynamic aggregate supply curve is similar to the aggregate supply curve we saw in Chapter 14, except that inflation rather than the price level is on the vertical axis. The DAS curve shows how inflation is related to output in the short run. Its upward slope reflects the Phillips curve: other things equal, higher levels of economic activity are associated with higher marginal costs of production and, therefore, higher inflation. The DAS curve is drawn for given values of past inflation pt 21 , the natural level of output Y – t , and the supply shock yt . If any one of these three variables changes, the DAS curve shifts. One of our tasks ahead is to trace out the implications of such shifts. But first, we need another curve.
